mid.name: Culinary Alchemy
entries: The azarpal knows the formulas for all common and uncommon alchemical foods of its level or lower in Treasure Vault without needing a formula book. A typical azarpal carries about 700 gp of alchemical food.

mid.name: Gulp or Grab
entries: The Azarpal swallows a single meal or alchemical food and stores it in one of six stomachs. Any item that remains stored in an azarpal's stomach for at least 24 hours becomes laced with azarpal poison.

entries: When an azarpal casts illusory disguise and only targets themselves, the duration increases to 24 hours.

mid.name: Twirl Tail
entries: The azarpal lashes and twirls their confounding tail, snapping and lashing it in all adjacent squares. Until the start of the azarpal's next turn, all non-azarpals treat the squares adjacent to the azarpal as difficult terrain.

_aon.markdown:
<title level="1" pfs="">[Azarpal](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3738)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Azarpals resemble bipedal hogs with wide-tusked mouths, bloated bellies, and long, bristly tails. They can store food in their multiple stomachs for long periods of time, slowly infusing it with a signature poison that causes those afflicted to sweat profusely and succumb to intense nausea.

 Azarpals love spreading discontent via poisoned food. They delight in traveling caravan routes, disguised as merchants, constantly sampling regional cuisines, and choosing their favorites for stomach storage and poison infusion. Then, upon reaching a land where the dish is rare or sought after, they find a place to leave the meal out for an unwary traveler. They might also find a way to introduce the poisoned meal to a tavern or restaurant and hang back to watch the resulting fun.

<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="">Removing Azarpal Poison</title>

Once an item of food or drink has been laced with azarpal poison, it can be detoxified through the use of a [_cleanse cuisine_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1468) spell or by spending an hour using alchemical supplies to nullify the poison. This latter option requires access to an [alchemical lab](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2701) and a successful [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) check against the azarpal's poison save DC.
</aside>

creature.name: Furnerico

mid.name: Fetid Aura
entries: 80 feet. A creature entering or beginning its turn in a furnerico's fetid aura must succeed at a DC 31 Fortitude or be sickened 1; the creature also becomes enfeebled 1 until the end of their next turn. A creature that succeeds at its save is temporarily immune to all furnerico fetid auras for 1 minute.

mid.name: Hydrophobic
entries: A furnerico avoids water and won't willingly approach within five feet of a body of water. It won't initiate an attack against any creature that's soaking wet with water or that has the water trait. A furnerico takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its attack rolls against such creatures who attack it.

mid.name: Susceptible to Water
entries: A furnerico cleansed of filth becomes sluggish. If ever immersed fully in pure, clean water, or if it ever fails a saving throw against a water effect, the furnerico becomes slowed 1 until it starts its turn in an area of filth or contaminated water.

mid.name: Feast on Illness
entries: The furnerico feeds off the sweet sickness of the creature, gaining 30 temporary hit points for 1 minute.

mid.name: Sticky Slime
entries: A creature that's critically hit by a furnerico's acidic slime becomes immobilized until they Escape (DC 34) or 1 minute passes, after which the slime dissolves.

_aon.markdown:
A mass of undulating tendrils and nerves, furnericos stalk sewer systems below large cities, reveling in the filth and rotting detritus created by those who dwell above the middens and sumps they call home. Fortunately for sanitation workers and other civil servants who ply their trade in sewer tunnels, furnericos are exceedingly rare and solitary. Their power is such that once one moves into a sewer system, it's often easier for urban planners to simply abandon that section to the monster and rebuild around it. A furnerico left to its domain like this is generally content to remain—as long as the filth keeps flowing. Furnericos are asexual, spawning a single offspring as they expire from natural causes. One that dies by violence does not perpetuate its kind, presenting a vexing question to sages: where do these creatures come from, and why haven't they gone extinct over the ages? **[Recall Knowledge - Aberration](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 37 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 35 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 32 [Furnerico](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3739) **Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 85 **Perception** +24; [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=74) ([precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411)) 60 feet **Languages** **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +28, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +25 **Str** +8 **Dex** +5 **Con** +8 **Int** -4 **Wis** +4 **Cha** -3 --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +28 **Ref** +23 **Will** +24 **HP** 320 **Immunities** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578) **Resistances** bludgeoning 15, piercing 15, [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) 15 **Weaknesses** slashing 15 **Fetid Aura** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=664)) 80 feet. A creature entering or beginning its turn in a furnerico's fetid aura must succeed at a DC 31 Fortitude or be [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91); the creature also becomes [enfeebled 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) until the end of their next turn. A creature that succeeds at its save is temporarily immune to all furnerico fetid auras for 1 minute.
**Hydrophobic** A furnerico avoids water and won't willingly approach within five feet of a body of water. It won't initiate an attack against any creature that's soaking wet with water or that has the [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732) trait. A furnerico takes a –2 circumstance penalty to its attack rolls against such creatures who attack it.
**Susceptible to Water** A furnerico cleansed of filth becomes sluggish. If ever immersed fully in pure, clean water, or if it ever fails a saving throw against a [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732) effect, the furnerico becomes [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) until it starts its turn in an area of filth or contaminated water. --- **Speed** 15 feet, climb 30 feet **Melee** pseudopod +28 ([reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 3d12+14 bludgeoning **Ranged** acidic slime +25 ([range 60 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=248)), **Damage** 4d6 acid plus 3d6 [persistent acid](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) **Feast on Illness** ([Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Requirements** The furnerico's last action was a successful pseudopod Strike against a creature with the [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) condition; **Effect** The furnerico feeds off the sweet sickness of the creature, gaining 30 temporary hit points for 1 minute. **Sticky Slime** A creature that's critically hit by a furnerico's acidic slime becomes [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) until they [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) (DC 34) or 1 minute passes, after which the slime dissolves.
Cultist Creations The answer to “where are furnericos from?” is known by only a few, for it lies with the faithful of the parasite god [Ghlaunder](/Deities.aspx?ID=343). These cultists use obscure rites to create furnericos from the very filth the monsters wallow in. Ghlaunder worshippers often do so to create powerful guardians for their hidden temples; furnericos created in this manner instinctively treat worshippers of Ghlaunder as allies... a trait not shared by those born from a prior furnerico, and a lesson many Ghlaunder cultists only learn moments before their death after assuming otherwise from a furnerico found in the wild.

mid.name: Brimstone Cloak
entries: 10 feet. The hellshadow constantly exudes a cloud of smoke that scorches flesh but leaves other materials unharmed. Living creatures who start their turn in this aura take 2d6 fire damage (DC 30 basic Reflex). On a critical failure, the creature is also sickened 1.

mid.name: Clinging Smoke
entries: A creature that takes damage from the hellshadow's brimstone tendrils Strike has coils of the creature's smoke solidify around their body, impeding movement. The creature must attempt a DC 33 Reflex save.

mid.name: Critical Success
entries: The creature is unaffected.

mid.name: Success
entries: The smoke solidifies as it coils around their limbs, imposing a –5-foot status penalty to all Speeds until the end of the creature's next turn.

mid.name: Failure
entries: As success, except –10 feet to speed and the creature is also clumsy 1 until the end of their next turn.

mid.name: Critical Failure
entries: As failure, except the creature is also slowed 1 until the end of their next turn.

_aon.markdown:
When a group of diabolists or worshippers of an archdevil come to an ignominious end, their souls can sometimes be caught between life and death, unable or unwilling to pass on to the afterlife due to the humiliation of their untimely deaths. When enough closely-associated worshippers whose souls aren't already claimed in existing contracts meet such a fate, the spiritual “weight” of this shame can cause them to merge into a conglomeration of infernally-infused spirits—a hellshadow. Hellshadows look like a bank of fire and smoke, yet the flames themselves are made of distorted bodies and faces. Although made of multiple souls, a hellshadow is a singular creature with one mind and typically one goal: to defeat as many enemies of their faith as they can in order to repay the shame of their humiliating deaths. **[Recall Knowledge - Fiend](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 36 **[Recall Knowledge - Undead](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Hellshadow](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3740) **Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 86 **Perception** +24; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Diabolic](/Languages.aspx?ID=117) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +25, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +27, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +25 **Str** -5 **Dex** +6 **Con** +5 **Int** +4 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +8 --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +23 **Ref** +25 **Will** +22 **HP** 175 ([void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83)) **Immunities** [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), precision, [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) **Resistances** all 10 (except [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610), [ghost touch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2840), or [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509); double resistance against non-[magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Weaknesses** [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) 10 **Brimstone Cloak** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [sanctified](/Traits.aspx?ID=519)) 10 feet. The hellshadow constantly exudes a cloud of smoke that scorches flesh but leaves other materials unharmed. Living creatures who start their turn in this aura take 2d6 fire damage (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex). On a critical failure, the creature is also [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91). --- **Speed** fly 40 feet **Melee** brimstone tendrils +27 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [Finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=602), [Fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [reach 15 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684), [Sanctified](/Traits.aspx?ID=519)), **Damage** 3d8+6 fire plus 2d6 void and clinging smoke **Divine Innate Spells** DC 33, attack +25 - **Cantrips (7th)** [Divine Lance](/Spells.aspx?ID=1498), [Void Warp](/Spells.aspx?ID=1745) - **6th** [Crisis of Faith](/Spells.aspx?ID=1478), [Divine Immolation](/Spells.aspx?ID=1496) - **7th** [Divine Decree](/Spells.aspx?ID=1495), [Shadow Blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=1666) (fire or spirit only) **Clinging Smoke** ([Divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579)) A creature that takes damage from the hellshadow's brimstone tendrils Strike has coils of the creature's smoke solidify around their body, impeding movement. The creature must attempt a DC 33 Reflex save.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The smoke solidifies as it coils around their limbs, imposing a –5-foot status penalty to all Speeds until the end of the creature's next turn.
**Failure** As success, except –10 feet to speed and the creature is also clumsy 1 until the end of their next turn.
**Critical Failure** As failure, except the creature is also slowed 1 until the end of their next turn.
Why Only Hell? The nature of diabolic worship and the strict rules involved are a big part of the psychology of humiliation that causes devil worshippers to become hellshadows. This same mix of conditions is rarer among other fiendish cults, who are more likely to become more common undead after such a death. Non-diabolic– themed hellshadows are all but unknown as a result.

creature.name: Ockomlire

mid.name: Emotion Vulnerability
entries: If an ockomlire fails a saving throw against an emotion effect, they loses their resistance to mental damage and gains an equal amount of weakness to mental damage (weakness to mental 15 for the typical ockomlire) until the end of their next turn.

mid.name: Devour Magic
entries: The ockomlire attempts to devour a spell effect from a creature they've grabbed. To successfully do so, they must counteract that effect with an Occultism check. If the spell effect is an emotion effect, the ockomlire gains a +2 circumstance bonus to this check.

mid.name: Critical Success
entries: The spell is countered, the ockomlire gains temporary Hit Points equal to twice the spell's rank for 1 minute, and the grabbed creature becomes stupefied 2 for 1 minute.

mid.name: Success
entries: As success but stupefied 1.

mid.name: Critical Failure
entries: The attempt backfires, and the ockomlire becomes overwhelmed; their emotion vulnerability becomes active until the end of their turn.

mid.name: Haze of Despair
entries: Requirements The ockomlire has temporary hit points gained from Devour Magic; Effects The ockomlire digests the magic and releases mist that stings the eyes and heart alike. The ockomlire loses any temporary Hit Points they have and all non-ockomlire creatures in a 30-foot emanation take 9d10 mental damage (DC 33 basic Will save).

_aon.markdown:
With its mottled green-and-tan rubbery flesh, six short legs ending in two-clawed feet, and three circular mouths arrayed equidistantly around a disk-shaped head crowned by multiple bulbous eyes, the bizarre Darklands-dwelling ockomlire's strange appearance blurs the line between aberration and fungus. Ockomlires eat magic, and their specialized organs process and release that magic in the form of a mist that saps the willpower of those it touches. Originally created by [sekmin](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=468) occultists as a potent weapon against Azlanti wizards, since the serpentfolk empire's collapse thousands of years ago, ockomlires have spread upward through the Darklands. They often lair in sewers or abandoned basements in urban areas, drawn to society's use (and waste) of magical energy. Ockomlires are quite intelligent but tend to have bland personalities. They're fond of verbalizing their observations and experiences, speaking in unsettling piping voices through three mouths; they have a curious penchant for referring to themselves in the third person. They've little interest in having personal names and tend to refer to those they encounter by ancestry instead of name as well. **[Recall Knowledge - Aberration](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Ockomlire](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3741) **Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 87 **Perception** +23; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13), [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1), [Sakvroth](/Languages.aspx?ID=118) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +24, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) +23 **Str** +8 **Dex** +4 **Con** +5 **Int** +5 **Wis** +4 **Cha** +0 --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +26 **Ref** +21 **Will** +23 +1 status to all saves vs [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590) effects **HP** 235 **Resistances** [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) 15 **Weaknesses** emotion vulnerability **Emotion Vulnerability** If an ockomlire fails a saving throw against an emotion effect, they loses their resistance to mental damage and gains an equal amount of weakness to mental damage (weakness to mental 15 for the typical ockomlire) until the end of their next turn. --- **Speed** 20 feet, climb 10 feet **Melee** jaws +27 ([Forceful](/Traits.aspx?ID=611)), **Damage** 3d10+14 piercing plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66) **Occult Innate Spells** DC 33 - **7th** [Calm](/Spells.aspx?ID=1458) (at will) - **Constant (7th)** [Detect Magic](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485) **Devour Magic** ([Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) The ockomlire attempts to devour a spell effect from a creature they've [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77). To successfully do so, they must [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) that effect with an [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) check. If the spell effect is an [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590) effect, the ockomlire gains a +2 circumstance bonus to this check.
**Critical Success** The spell is countered, the ockomlire gains temporary Hit Points equal to twice the spell's rank for 1 minute, and the grabbed creature becomes [stupefied 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) for 1 minute.
**Success** As success but stupefied 1.
**Critical Failure** The attempt backfires, and the ockomlire becomes overwhelmed; their emotion vulnerability becomes active until the end of their turn. **Haze of Despair** ([Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Requirements** The ockomlire has temporary hit points gained from Devour Magic; **Effects** The ockomlire digests the magic and releases mist that stings the eyes and heart alike. The ockomlire loses any temporary Hit Points they have and all non-ockomlire creatures in a 30-foot emanation take 9d10 mental damage (DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Will save).
Ockomlire Apathy Because they exude feelings of hopelessness and despair as “waste” from their magical feeding, the ockomlire has become a creature of apathetic detachment. While this affords the ockomlire protection from emotion-based effects, those that do affect them tend to hit hard and actually cause mental anguish. There are thrilling legends of ockomlires laid low by a single bard whose gripping performance simply stirred up enough emotions within the normally distant creatures to cause them rip themselves apart from the inside.

mid.name: Glutton Scent
entries: A rezzelki's scent ability becomes a precise sense against its favored meal.

mid.name: Favored Meal
entries: All rezzelkis have a favorite type of creature to feast upon (see the Rezzelki Hunger sidebar). Against a favored meal in combat, a rezzelki gains a +1 circumstance bonus to all Strikes and Athletics checks.

mid.name: Reactive Taste
mid.trigger: A creature within reach of the rezzelki's tongue uses a manipulate or a move action, makes a ranged attack, or leaves a square during a move action it's using
entries: The rezzelki makes a tongue Strike against the triggering creature.

mid.name: Fracturing Smash
entries: The rezzelki Strikes a target with a particularly powerful blow from its tail, with enough force to potentially pulverize bone. This Strike treats any object it hits as if it had half as much Hardness as usual, unless the object's hardness is greater than the rezzelki's level. If the Fracturing Smash hits, it deals two extra dice of weapon damage. A creature with a skeleton that takes damage must succeed at a DC 26 Fortitude save or become clumsy 1 (clumsy 2 on a critical failure) by the Fracturing Smash as its bones are partially broken.

_aon.markdown:
Rezzelkis are curious-looking beasts native to the deserts of Osirion. Three feet tall at the shoulder and five feet long, rezzelkis are squat, mammalian quadrupeds with tawny red fur, with crystal-studded flat tails, and prehensile anteater-like snouts. Their long, pink tongues are covered with hundreds of tiny, razor-sharp bristles that allow them to rasp through flesh with unnerving ease, even before accounting for the effect of their acidic saliva. Rezzelkis are ferociously territorial and quick to attack anyone or anything they regard as intruding upon their territory. Yet they're also prone to strange gastronomic obsessions, and if someone can deduce a particular rezzelki's favorite food, it's possible to become the creature's ally by simply providing it regular access to its preferred meals. A specific rezzelki's favorite food is always a specific type of creature— some even prefer to dine exclusively on the dry bodies of undead like [mummies](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=445)—but most have a taste for a singular humanoid ancestry. Presented with a potential meal, the rezzelki moves quickly to smash its feast with its wide tail. Then it feeds upon the pulverized remains of the destroyed creature, slurping up battered flesh and powdered bones with a noisy gusto that has earned them a strange nickname in certain circles: “deathlicker.” **[Recall Knowledge - Beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43)): DC 29 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 27 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 24 [Rezzelki](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3742) **Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 88 **Perception** +21; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59), glutton scent ([imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412)) 60 feet **Languages** [Osiriani](/Languages.aspx?ID=40); (can't speak) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +22 **Str** +6 **Dex** +3 **Con** +5 **Int** -3 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +2 **Glutton Scent** A rezzelki's scent ability becomes a [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) sense against its favored meal. --- **AC** 29 **Fort** +21 **Ref** +17 **Will** +19 **HP** 175 **Resistances** [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524) 10 **Favored Meal** All rezzelkis have a favorite type of creature to feast upon (see the Rezzelki Hunger sidebar). Against a favored meal in combat, a rezzelki gains a +1 circumstance bonus to all Strikes and [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) checks.
**Reactive Taste** ([primal](/Traits.aspx?ID=676)) **Trigger** A creature within reach of the rezzelki's tongue uses a [manipulate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2229) or a [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658) action, makes a ranged attack, or leaves a square during a move action it's using; **Effect** The rezzelki makes a tongue Strike against the triggering creature. --- **Speed** 25 feet, fly 20 feet **Melee** tail +22 ([Forceful](/Traits.aspx?ID=611)), **Damage** 2d12+10 bludgeoning plus [Knockdown](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=46) **Melee** tongue +22 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526), [reach 10 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=684)), **Damage** 2d6+6 slashing plus 1d6 acid **Primal Innate Spells** DC 29 - **Constant (5th)** [Fly](/Spells.aspx?ID=1534) **Fracturing Smash** ([Attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=540)) The rezzelki Strikes a target with a particularly powerful blow from its tail, with enough force to potentially pulverize bone. This Strike treats any object it hits as if it had half as much Hardness as usual, unless the object's hardness is greater than the rezzelki's level. If the Fracturing Smash hits, it deals two extra dice of weapon damage. A creature with a skeleton that takes damage must succeed at a DC 26 Fortitude save or become [clumsy 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) (clumsy 2 on a critical failure) by the Fracturing Smash as its bones are partially broken.
Rezzelki Hunger While a rezzelki can subsist on any sort of pulverized creature's remains, they vastly prefer a specific type of creature and can sniff these potential meals out with alarming accuracy. If an encounter doesn't specify what a rezzelki's favorite foodstuff is, roll 1d6: 1—[human](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=6), 2—[dwarf](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=1), 3—[elf](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=2), 4—[kholo](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=79), 5—[desert giant](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1167), 6—[mummy](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=445). Rezzelkis found in regions other than Osirion certainly develop appetites for other types of creatures, of course!

creature.name: Anguish Siktempora

mid.name: Temporal Sense
entries: A siktempora can always roll Dimension of Time Lore for initiative. When it does, it gains a +2 circumstance bonus to the roll.

mid.name: Foster Fear
entries: Creatures with the frightened condition are always off-guard to the anguish siktempora.

mid.name: Uncanny Pounce
mid.trigger: The anguish siktempora rolls Dimension of Time Lore for initiative
entries: The siktempora Strides once and makes a jaws Strike, in either order.

mid.name: Scream of Despair
entries: The anguish siktempora emits a terrible scream in a 30-foot emanation. Creatures in the area must attempt a DC 33 Will save. The anguish siktempora can't use Scream of Despair for 1d4 rounds. Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

mid.name: Success
entries: The creature takes 2d6 mental damage, 2d6 sonic damage, and is frightened 1.

mid.name: Failure
entries: The creature takes 6d6 mental damage, 6d6 sonic damage, and is frightened 2.

mid.name: Critical Failure
entries: As failure, but frightened 3 and the creature gains weakness to mental 15 (this weakness applies to this Scream of Despair).

mid.name: Wracking Despair
entries: The anguish siktempora projects their crippling despair into the mind of a frightened creature they can see within range of their telepathy. The frightened creature takes 6d6 mental damage (DC 30 basic Will save).

_aon.markdown:
Across the crooked folds of the [Dimension of Time](/Planes.aspx?ID=46), intense emotions gather like flotsam in the still waters of river pools. These accumulate over ages, harvesting stronger feelings during times of great change such as calamities and the rule of tyrannical despots, as well as periods of joy and pride. These accretions eventually give birth to siktemporas. The anguish siktempora is rare, even among others of their kind. They delight in seeking out creatures to inflict their suffering upon, the utterances of their dreadful wails relieve their anguish—if only for a fleeting moment. With a huge, malformed human head gaping in the act of screaming, their sickly hook-ended limbs hang limply below the neck. When an anguish siktempora bites foes with their jaws, they continue screaming, adding sonic damage to the already crushing punishment their numerous grinding teeth inflict. **[Recall Knowledge - Time](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Anguish Siktempora](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3743) **Source** [Pathfinder #204: Stage Fright](/Sources.aspx?ID=245) pg. 89 **Perception** +26; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Aklo](/Languages.aspx?ID=13); (can't speak any language); [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) 300 feet **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +24, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +27, [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) +24, [Dimension of Time Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +26, [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +24 **Str** +8 **Dex** +5 **Con** +5 **Int** +5 **Wis** +7 **Cha** +5 **Temporal Sense** A siktempora can always roll [Dimension of Time Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) for initiative. When it does, it gains a +2 circumstance bonus to the roll. --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +24 **Ref** +22 **Will** +26 **HP** 180 , regeneration 40 (deactivated by [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [orichalcum](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2859), or [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737)) **Immunities** [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) **Foster Fear** Creatures with the frightened condition are always off-guard to the anguish siktempora.
**Uncanny Pounce** **Trigger** The anguish siktempora rolls [Dimension of Time Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) for initiative; **Effect** The siktempora Strides once and makes a jaws Strike, in either order. --- **Speed** 10 feet, fly 40 feet **Melee** jaws +27, **Damage** 3d6+14 bludgeoning plus 2d6 sonic **Melee** claw +27 ([Agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526)), **Damage** 3d8+14 slashing **Occult Innate Spells** DC 33 - **4th** [Translocate](/Spells.aspx?ID=1724) (at will) - **7th** [Flicker](/Spells.aspx?ID=1532) - **Constant (7th)** [Fly](/Spells.aspx?ID=1534) **[Rend](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=73)** claw **Scream of Despair** ([Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662), [Sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697)) The anguish siktempora emits a terrible scream in a 30-foot emanation. Creatures in the area must attempt a DC 33 Will save. The anguish siktempora can't use Scream of Despair for 1d4 rounds. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 2d6 mental damage, 2d6 sonic damage, and is [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76).
**Failure** The creature takes 6d6 mental damage, 6d6 sonic damage, and is frightened 2.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but frightened 3 and the creature gains weakness to [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) 15 (this weakness applies to this Scream of Despair). **Wracking Despair** ([Emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [Mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Frequency** once per round; **Effect** The anguish siktempora projects their crippling despair into the mind of a frightened creature they can see within range of their telepathy. The frightened creature takes 6d6 mental damage (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Will save).
Soaked In Screams The anguish siktempora, sometimes called a living scream, forms from similar emotions that generate misery siktemporas. Where disasters and devastation occur, so too do both of these creatures manifest— often compounding the ambient pain and bloating the siktemporas accordingly. Occasionally, misery and anguish siktempora fight each other over territory in such moments, literally pulling their rivals limb from limb in an unquenchable need to feed adjacent hungers.
